title: Lifting an arbitrary perfect open-site stalk chain map
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U$ an affine open, $x\in U$, and $P,Q$ strictly perfect complexes of module sheaves on the slice site over $U$ [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Write $T$ for the termwise open module stalk functor at $x$ [def-sc-open-module-stalk-functor]. Every chain map $t:T(P)\to T(Q)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is represented on an affine open $V\subseteq U$ containing $x$: for the restriction functor $R$ from $U$ to $V$ and the termwise stalk functor $S$ at $x$ on $V$, there exist a natural isomorphism $e:R\circ S\cong T$ (composition in functor order) and a chain map $g:R(P)\to R(Q)$ with $S(g)=e_P\,t\,e_Q^{-1}$ (composition in categorical order). No homotopy inverse or quasi-isomorphism of $t$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09RE, affine proof case (1), finite-component calculation; More on Algebra Tag 0BC7 (2); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09RE and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BC7

proof.text: Apply degreewise extension to the components of the given chain map t, obtaining W and g with their stalk identities in the canonical restriction comparison eW. Only strict perfectness of P is used.

Conjugating t by the canonical eW gives a chain map. Its adjacent equations and the component identities of g prove that the stalks of g commute with the differentials. Apply the source degreewise shrinking theorem using its canonical comparisons eW and eV, obtaining V and chain-compatible components k with the prescribed stalk formula.

Construct fV with CochainComplex.ofHom k hk. Check the desired stalk equality degreewise with HomologicalComplex.hom_ext. Substitute the stalk identities of k and g and cancel the middle inverse/hom comparison pairs by associativity. This proves the source theorem with the canonical eV. Choosing eV also proves the original node existence statement, and the original extra assumptions on U and Q are unused.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_affine_perfect_open_stalk_chainMap_lift
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens) (x : X) (hxU : x ∈ U)
    (P Q : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hP : IsStrictlyPerfect X U P)
    (t : ((openModuleStalkFunctor X U ⟨x, hxU⟩).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P ⟶
      ((openModuleStalkFunctor X U ⟨x, hxU⟩).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q) :
    ∃ (V : X.Opens) (hxV : x ∈ V) (_hV : IsAffineOpen V) (hVU : V ≤ U),
      let R := (SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)
        (homOfLE hVU : V ⟶ U)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
      let S := (openModuleStalkFunctor X V ⟨x, hxV⟩).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
      let T := (openModuleStalkFunctor X U ⟨x, hxU⟩).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
      let e : R ⋙ S ≅ T := Functor.mapHomologicalComplexCompIso
        (openModuleStalkRestrictionComparison X U V hVU x hxU hxV) (.up ℤ)
      ∃ g : R.obj P ⟶ R.obj Q,
        S.map g = (e.app P).hom ≫ t ≫ (e.app Q).inv
lean.note: Retired the duplicate Sheaf theorem. The existing proved source theorem supplies the canonical comparison and requires neither affineness of U nor strict perfectness of Q. Choosing that comparison and ignoring the extra original hypotheses proves the unchanged node statement. Both direct consumers keep their exact public signatures and explicitly name the canonical comparison. The node and all dependency edges remain.
